title: Enumerate in-flight foundation attempts from the durable store
description:
Objective: produce the `InFlightAttempt[]` that restart reconciliation consumes. Prerequisite of task-3e54b466da3d4385ae9fbbf886a45464 (Run restart reconciliation from the daemon boot path), discovered at ITS planning time.

MEASURED GAP at HEAD e881141. `reconcileOnRestart` (recovery/restart-reconciliation.ts:235) takes `RestartReconciliationRequest` = `{attempts: readonly InFlightAttempt[], correlationId, decidedAt, principalId, projectId}` (:60-66), where `InFlightAttempt` = `{attemptRef: string, situation: unknown}` (:32-35). NOTHING PRODUCES THAT ARRAY: `grep -rn "InFlightAttempt" --include=*.ts apps/daemon/src` returns only its own declaration and its use inside the request type. So the boot sweep cannot be wired until something can answer "which attempts were in flight when we died".

WHY THIS IS NOT PART OF THE WIRING TASK. Wiring is a consumer edge — call a complete capability and fail closed. This is NEW production capability: a durable reader with its own fold, its own refusals and its own tests. Merging them would have made the wiring task edit what it composes, which its own rails forbid.

MEASURED VOCABULARY, so the reader is not guessed:
- `FOUNDATION_DISPATCH_EVENT_TYPES` (work/foundation-attempt-contracts.ts:47) = `{RECORDED: "FoundationAttemptRecorded", RESERVED: "FoundationDispatchReserved"}`. Exactly two members.
- `FOUNDATION_DISPATCH_COMMAND_KIND` = "foundation.dispatch" (:39).
- Existing single-attempt readers, all keyed by a known id and therefore unusable for enumeration: `readStoredFoundationAttempt` (work/foundation-attempt-store.ts:128), `readFoundationAttemptRecord` (:149), `readDurableFoundationObservation` (:73), `readFoundationReservationDigest` (:115). Reuse their decode/drift discipline rather than re-deriving it — `readStoredFoundationAttempt` re-encodes the decoded payload and compares bytes, refusing `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_DRIFT` on mismatch. The enumerator must not be laxer.
- Bounded paging landed this cycle: `readEventsByTypeAfter` on the public store (sqlite-event-store.ts:354, delegated at decision-ledger.ts:77/148), index-backed by `domain_events_event_type_position`. Use it — do NOT walk all project events.

THE DESIGN QUESTION THIS TASK MUST ANSWER FROM THE DURABLE RECORD, not invent: `FOUNDATION_DISPATCH_EVENT_TYPES` names no terminal/completion member, so "still in flight" cannot be read off that map alone. Determine it from committed evidence — e.g. a RESERVED without its RECORDED, or a recorded attempt with no later terminal marker in whatever aggregate owns one — and pin the rule in the module comment. If the durable record genuinely cannot distinguish in-flight from finished, that is a real gap: report blocked with the missing evidence named, rather than inferring liveness from absence.

`situation` is typed `unknown` because `classifyCrash` validates it internally. Populate it from committed evidence only; never from a caller claim or a clock guess.

NOT in scope: calling `reconcileOnRestart` (task-3e54b466 owns that), the coordination command kind (task-d17bb228), the pinned Claude spawn chain, or changing restart-reconciliation.ts.

Owned paths: one new module under apps/daemon/src/work/ or apps/daemon/src/recovery/ plus its .js bridge and its .test.ts.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test — read the OUTPUT count line, not the exit code. Daemon gates are red at baseline from foreign slices; apply the path-attributed baseline over the owned paths.
definitionOfDone: A production reader returns `readonly InFlightAttempt[]` from a real SqliteEventStore, and `grep -rn "InFlightAttempt" --include=*.ts apps/daemon/src | grep -v '\.test\.'` shows a producer in addition to the type declaration and the request field — the producer count was zero before this task.

The in-flight rule is stated in the module comment and asserted: a test seeds attempts in each committed state and asserts exactly which are returned and which are not, so "in flight" is a decided property of the record rather than an inference from absence.

Enumeration is BOUNDED and index-backed: it pages via `readEventsByTypeAfter` and a test asserts the number of events read is proportional to attempt events, not to total project events — with a literal bound that a full-stream walk would fail.

Decode drift is refused, not skipped: an attempt whose payload does not re-encode to the same bytes yields the exact stable code and layer that `readStoredFoundationAttempt` already uses for that condition, and the sweep does NOT silently omit it — an undecodable attempt is never treated as finished.
`situation` is populated only from committed evidence; a test asserts no caller-supplied value and no clock reading can reach it, and a mutation feeding a caller value turns a NAMED test red.

A refusal pins the exact stable code AND the answering layer; where the store and the attempt decoder can both refuse, the fixture is valid at the store layer so the decoder is provably the one that answered.

Real SqliteEventStore in tests, opened per test and closed in a `finally` on every exit path; production source under 250 physical lines by `grep -c ''`, with a one-line LF .js bridge; apps/daemon/src/index.ts unmodified.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` run with exit codes captured separately; the test leg prints a nonzero Test Files/Tests count line, and the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta over the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: Decide `in flight` from committed evidence and write the rule down. If the durable record cannot distinguish in-flight from finished, report blocked naming the missing evidence — never infer liveness from the absence of a marker, which would classify every finished attempt as a crash.

Do not modify restart-reconciliation.ts, foundation-attempt-store.ts or foundation-attempt-contracts.ts. Reuse their decode/drift discipline; `readStoredFoundationAttempt` re-encodes and byte-compares before trusting a payload, and this reader must not be laxer.
Page with `readEventsByTypeAfter`. Walking all project events to filter by type is the O(total events) defect task-16d5bc3a exists to remove; do not reintroduce it here.
Fail closed: an undecodable or drifted attempt is refused with its stable code and layer, never silently omitted from the sweep. An omitted attempt is an attempt nobody will reconcile.
Real SqliteEventStore in tests, closed in a `finally` on every exit path — a held handle kills the vitest worker. Preserve foreign work; commit only owned paths by pathspec.

implementationPlan.description:
BASELINE, AND TAKE THE IN-FLIGHT RULE FROM PRODUCTION — it is already written down, so do not invent one. This task's description flags "how do we know an attempt is still in flight" as the open design question. Planning it found the answer already stated in `foundation-attempt-service.ts:218-224`, in the dispatch replay path:
  "A REPLAYED reservation NEVER launches. It adopts the durable final record or says the dispatch is still in flight; a missing record is not an invitation to start a second process."
  `if (reserved.disposition === "REPLAYED") { const adopted = readStoredFoundationAttempt(store, bound.target); return adopted.ok || adopted.code !== "FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_ABSENT" ? adopted : refuseLocal("FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_DISPATCH_IN_PROGRESS"); }`
THE RULE, therefore: **a `FoundationDispatchReserved` with no `FoundationAttemptRecorded` in the same aggregate is still in flight.** That is production's existing semantics for one attempt; this task generalises it to all of them. Write that citation into the module comment — it is what stops a later reader re-deriving a different rule, and it is why this is not an inference from absence.
Re-confirm on current bytes (measured at HEAD 0f19e06): `FOUNDATION_DISPATCH_EVENT_TYPES` (work/foundation-attempt-contracts.ts:47) = `{RECORDED: "FoundationAttemptRecorded", RESERVED: "FoundationDispatchReserved"}`, exactly two members; `commitFoundationPhase` (foundation-attempt-store.ts:99) writes them with `tag: "RECORDED" | "RESERVED"` onto `bound.target`; `InFlightAttempt` = `{attemptRef, situation}` (restart-reconciliation.ts:32) and still has ZERO producers.
GATES, each run separately with its own exit code — never `;`-chained (only the last status survives), never piped into tail (tail's status is reported): `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, recording the count line and every failing file as your before-set. Both are expected RED from foreign in-flight slices; repair none of it.

VOCABULARY RE-CONFIRMED ON CURRENT BYTES:
- `FOUNDATION_DISPATCH_EVENT_TYPES` (work/foundation-attempt-contracts.ts:47) = `{RECORDED: "FoundationAttemptRecorded", RESERVED: "FoundationDispatchReserved"}`, exactly two members.

Also measured for step 3/4: `readEventsByTypeAfter(eventType, afterGlobalPosition, limit?, maxDecodedBytes?)` on SqliteEventStore (sqlite-event-store.ts:354) returning `CursorPage<StoredEvent,bigint>` = `{hasMore, items, nextCursor}`; `StoredEvent` carries `aggregateId`, `globalPosition`, `eventType`, `payload`, `decisionTrace?.projectId`. implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, PART 1 — the rule and its ambiguity arms. Create the enumerator's test against the not-yet-existing module and let it fail to resolve. Seed a REAL SqliteEventStore with attempts in each committed state and assert exactly which are returned:
- RESERVED, no RECORDED -> IN FLIGHT, returned.
- RESERVED then RECORDED -> finished, NOT returned.
- RECORDED with no RESERVED -> not in flight; assert what it does explicitly rather than leaving it to fall through, since this shape means a reservation was lost and silently dropping it hides that.
- Neither -> absent, not returned.
That set is the DoD's "in-flight rule is a decided property of the record" — assert the returned set by exact attemptRefs, not by count.
AMBIGUITY AND DRIFT ARE REFUSALS, NOT SKIPS. The existing readers already fix these codes and the enumerator must not be laxer: `readFoundationReservationDigest` (foundation-attempt-store.ts:115) requires `found.length === 1` and answers null otherwise; `readStoredFoundationAttempt` (:128) refuses `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_AMBIGUOUS` for more than one RECORDED, `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_ABSENT` for none, and `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_DRIFT` when the decoded payload does not re-encode to the same bytes. Pin each with its exact code AND the answering layer. An undecodable or duplicated attempt must NOT be silently omitted — an omitted attempt is an attempt nobody will reconcile, which is worse than a loud refusal.
Also pin `situation`: it is populated only from the decoded reservation's committed fields. Assert that no caller-supplied value and no clock reading can reach it.

I hold the claim, so I proceeded rather than racing; I will re-check `git status --porcelain` before committing.

THE RULE ARMS, each asserted by exact attemptRefs and never by count:
- RESERVED with no RECORDED -> IN FLIGHT. `returns exactly the reservations whose record is absent` seeds `attempt-flying` (RESERVED only) and `attempt-finished` (RESERVED then RECORDED) and asserts `attempts.map(a => a.attemptRef)` toStrictEqual `["attempt-flying"]`.
- RESERVED then RECORDED -> finished, NOT returned. Same test; the finished ref is absent from that exact array.
- RECORDED with no RESERVED -> explicitly REPORTED, not dropped: `reports a record with no reservation as orphaned instead of dropping it` asserts `attempts` is `[]` AND `orphanedRecordAggregates` toStrictEqual `[orphan.target]`. A lost reservation is surfaced rather than absorbed into the general not-in-flight case.
- Neither phase -> absent from both arrays (`returns nothing for an attempt that committed neither phase`).

REFUSALS PIN CODE **AND** ANSWERING LAYER (toStrictEqual on `{code, refusedBy}`, so a wrong layer cannot pass):
- Drift: `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_DRIFT` / `DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT`. LAYER PROOF per the DoD: `seedDriftedReservation` writes non-canonical (unsorted-key) JSON through the production writer `commitFoundationPhase` and the test asserts `written.decision.effectDisposition === "EFFECTS_COMMITTED"` plus `store.readEvents(target)` length 1 — the fixture is valid at the STORE layer, so the re-encode byte comparison is provably the layer that answered. `canonical()` (foundation-attempt-codec.ts:131-145) sorts keys, which is what makes unsorted input decode fine and re-encode to different bytes.
- Ambiguity: two RESERVED on one aggregate (second committed at expectedVersion 1 under a distinct commandId) -> `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_AMBIGUOUS` / `DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT`. Not "resolve to the first".
- Neither refusal case may silently omit: both assert `sweep.ok === false`, i.e. the whole sweep refuses rather than returning a shorter list.

SITUATION PROVENANCE: `populates situation only from decoded committed reservation fields` calls the reader with a caller-supplied `pageLimit` of 7 and asserts `situation` toStrictEqual exactly `{...reservationBody, reservationDigest}` — an exact-key/exact-value comparison, so a merged caller value or an injected clock reading adds or changes a key and reddens.
FAIL-CLOSED DIRECTION PINNED: `hands classifyCrash a situation it refuses rather than one that gains authority` asserts `classifyCrash(situation)` answers `kind:"REFUSED"`, `failure.code:"RECOVERY_OBSERVATION_MALFORMED"`, `failure.layer:"CLASSIFICATION"`. A reservation carries no lease epoch and no process observation, so the honest answer is a situation the classifier refuses — NOT classifier-shaped fields manufactured to satisfy `SITUATION_KEYS` (crash-classification.ts:82).

Step-3's two cost/termination tests are in the same file and are addressed in step 3.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, PART 2 — enumeration must be BOUNDED and index-backed, and the assertion must fail against a full-stream walk. Task-69c2c9e7 landed `readEventsByTypeAfter` on the public store (sqlite-event-store.ts:354, delegated at decision-ledger.ts:77/148), index-backed by `domain_events_event_type_position`. Use it.
THE SHAPE THAT AVOIDS N+1: page `FoundationDispatchReserved` and page `FoundationAttemptRecorded` — two type-filtered walks — and take the set difference by `aggregateId`. Do NOT page reservations and then call a per-attempt reader for each one; that is one store round trip per reservation and it degrades exactly as the ledger grows. `StoredEvent` carries `aggregateId`, so the difference is computable from the two pages alone.
Write the cost assertion with a literal bound that TODAY'S alternatives would fail: count store reads through a counting port wrapper, seed a ledger where attempt events are a small fraction of total events, and assert the read count is proportional to attempt events rather than to the stream. Verify the assertion reddens against a deliberately-written full-stream version BEFORE implementing the real one — a cost bound that passes both shapes proves nothing.
Also assert the walk terminates and is bounded: pages are driven by `nextCursor` until the pager reports no more, with no unbounded loop and no reliance on a page happening to be short.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED PART 2. The cost assertion is proven able to tell the two shapes apart BEFORE the real reader was written.

ADOPTED TEST FILE, NOT MINE. Mid-step the parallel session rewrote apps/daemon/src/work/in-flight-attempts.test.ts wholesale with a stronger fixture set (file-backed SqliteEventStore.openForProject under mkdtempSync instead of the in-memory store, seeds through the production writer commitFoundationPhase, a global-stream walk helper to prove the noise was really written). Per the shared-worktree rule I adopted the bytes rather than racing or reverting, and I VERIFIED them by running them. It pins a different and stronger API than my draft, which is what I implemented against:
- signature `readInFlightFoundationAttempts(store, projectId)`; `attemptRef` is the DISPATCH aggregate id straight off StoredEvent.aggregateId.
- RECORDED with no RESERVED is a REFUSAL, `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_DISPATCH_SUSPECT`, not an orphan report — a final record with no reservation means the durable chain is broken, and refusing is the fail-closed reading of "handled explicitly rather than falling through".
- adds a duplicated-RECORDED arm (AMBIGUOUS, matching readStoredFoundationAttempt:136), a project fence (`FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_BINDING_MISMATCH`), a throwing-store arm and an empty-store arm.
- `IN_FLIGHT_SITUATION_KEYS` is exported and the provenance test asserts `Object.keys(situation)` toStrictEqual it, so key ORDER is load-bearing.
I made ONE correction to it: the classifyCrash expectation omitted `ok: false`, which `recoveryFailure` (recovery-contract.ts:178) puts on every failure. Received-vs-expected diff was a single `+ "ok": false`. Fixed the expectation; production was not touched for it.

THE CONTROL, AND ITS RED. I wrote in-flight-attempts.ts with `indexByAggregate` deliberately walking the GLOBAL stream (`store.readEventsAfter(cursor, 100)`) and filtering `event.eventType !== eventType` in memory — the exact defect task-16d5bc3a exists to remove — and ran the suite:
  `AssertionError: expected 168 to be less than or equal to 8` at in-flight-attempts.test.ts:333 (`expect(served).toBeLessThanOrEqual(8)`).
168 = two full walks over 84 events. The bound is therefore tight enough to distinguish the shapes; it is not a bound both shapes satisfy. `Test Files 1 failed (1)`, `Tests 2 failed | 10 passed (12)` — the 10 passing are the rule and refusal arms, which the full-stream control gets RIGHT, which is precisely why only a cost assertion can catch it.

THE COST FIXTURE IS ASSERTED TO EXIST, not assumed: the test walks the global stream itself and asserts `expect(stream).toHaveLength(84)` and `expect(stream.length).toBeGreaterThan(80)` before counting. A sweep that silently seeded zero noise would fail there rather than passing vacuously.
THE N+1 SHAPE IS ALSO EXCLUDED: the counting fake counts `readEvents` separately and the test asserts `expect(aggregateReads).toBe(0)`, so paging reservations and then calling a per-attempt reader for each is caught even though it would satisfy `served`.
TERMINATION: `refuses a pager that never advances instead of spinning on it` drives a fake returning `{hasMore:true, items:[], nextCursor:0n}` forever and requires `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_AMBIGUOUS`/`DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT`. The loop is driven by nextCursor with a strict-increase guard, so it does not rely on a page happening to be short. `refuses an unreadable durable store rather than reporting nothing in flight` covers the throwing pager with the same code, following the precedent at readStoredFoundationAttempt:132-133 where a store read fault answers AMBIGUOUS.

Also landed: the one-line LF `.js` bridge, byte-verified with `od -c` -> `export * from "./in-flight-attempts.ts";\n`, no CRLF and no trailing blank line.
The full-stream control is REPLACED in step 4; it is not the shipped implementation.

SHAPE. `readInFlightFoundationAttempts(store: SqliteEventStore, projectId: string): InFlightAttemptSweep` — `{ok:true, attempts: readonly InFlightAttempt[]}` or an EXISTING stable refusal from the closed FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_CODES list. No new code was minted, so foundation-attempt-contracts.ts stayed untouched.
- Captures `store.readEventHorizon()` ONCE, then walks `FoundationDispatchReserved` and `FoundationAttemptRecorded` via `readEventsByTypeAfter(type, cursor, 100)`, set-differenced by `aggregateId`. No global-stream walk and no per-reservation `readEvents` round trip — the test asserts `aggregateReads === 0` directly.
- `attemptRef` is `StoredEvent.aggregateId` (the dispatch aggregate), i.e. committed evidence read straight off the durable row rather than re-derived.

CONVERGED-ON DESIGN, NOT MINE ALONE. The parallel session rewrote the production module between my step-3 control and this step. I verified rather than adopted blindly: it composes `tracedProject` from apps/daemon/src/activation/foundation-binding-predicates.ts:38, which I checked is an ALREADY-COMMITTED production predicate (git status shows only my three untracked owned files; it is used at activation-ledger-reader.ts:155). So the project fence is reuse of a shipped predicate, not a new one, and it is strictly better than the store-health check I had drafted: it fences PER EVENT on `decisionTrace.projectId`, and it fails closed when `decisionTrace` is absent.

DECODE DISCIPLINE IS NOT LAXER THAN THE SINGLE-ATTEMPT READER. `situationOf` decodes, RE-ENCODES with `encodeFoundationPayload` and byte-compares with `sameBytes`, refusing FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_DRIFT on mismatch — the same three lines as readStoredFoundationAttempt:139-144 — then additionally requires `recordVersion === FOUNDATION_RESERVATION_VERSION` and that every one of the 8 committed keys is present as text, refusing DRIFT otherwise.

TERMINATION IS PROVED, NOT ASSUMED. The walk is `while (cursor < horizon)` with four independent guards, each refusing rather than spinning: a non-increasing `globalPosition` within a page, a page whose positions never advanced while `hasMore` is true, a `nextCursor` that disagrees with the last position read, and an event whose type is not the requested one. Growth past the captured horizon is deliberately out of the answer — a match beyond H is neither returned nor counted, so the walk cannot be extended indefinitely by concurrent writers.

`situation` PROVENANCE. Built by ALLOW-LIST over `IN_FLIGHT_SITUATION_KEYS` (the exact 8 fields the service commits at foundation-attempt-service.ts:209-214), never by spread, from the DECODED payload only. The two caller-supplied arguments are the store and the projectId; the projectId is used solely by the `tracedProject` fence and the test asserts `JSON.stringify(situation)` does not contain it. No clock is read anywhere in the file — the test runs the sweep twice over the same bytes and asserts byte-identical situations.

The two pre-existing ones are unchanged (restart-reconciliation.ts:32 declaration, :61 request field); the six NEW ones are all in work/in-flight-attempts.ts, including the PRODUCER `const attempts: InFlightAttempt[] = []` at :161 populated at :166 and returned at :168. implementationPlan.description:
MUTATION DRILLS — prove the rule, the refusals and the bound are each load-bearing. Run each alone, revert before the next. (1) Invert the rule so a RESERVED **with** a RECORDED counts as in flight; the finished-attempt case must redden — this is the drill that proves the enumerator implements the cited production semantics rather than something adjacent. (2) Make a drifted payload be SKIPPED instead of refused; the drift case must redden on its exact code and layer — a silently omitted attempt is one nobody reconciles, so a green here would mean the sweep can lose work invisibly. (3) Make a duplicate RESERVED resolve to the first entry instead of refusing; the ambiguity case must redden. (4) Replace the two type-filtered walks with a full-stream walk that filters in memory; the step-3 cost assertion must redden — if it stays green the bound was never tight enough to distinguish the shapes and must be tightened before completion. (5) Feed `situation` from a caller-supplied value; the provenance case must redden.
For EVERY drill record the exact replaced range you edited: a drill that applied nothing reads as green and proves nothing. Confirm each red lands on the INTENDED assertion, not on an unrelated crash or compile error. planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD 0f19e06. I filed this task 15 minutes ago while planning task-3e54b466, flagging one open design question: `FOUNDATION_DISPATCH_EVENT_TYPES` has no terminal member, so how is "still in flight" decided? Planning it FOUND THE ANSWER ALREADY IN PRODUCTION, which turns this from a design task into a generalisation task.

THE RULE, LIFTED NOT INVENTED. `foundation-attempt-service.ts:218-224`, the dispatch replay path:
  "A REPLAYED reservation NEVER launches. It adopts the durable final record or says the dispatch is still in flight; a missing record is not an invitation to start a second process."
  `if (reserved.disposition === "REPLAYED") { const adopted = readStoredFoundationAttempt(store, bound.target); return adopted.ok || adopted.code !== "FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_ABSENT" ? adopted : refuseLocal("FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_DISPATCH_IN_PROGRESS"); }`
So production ALREADY decides in-flight as: a reservation whose durable final record is ABSENT. Generalised: a `FoundationDispatchReserved` with no `FoundationAttemptRecorded` in the same aggregate. The module header must carry this citation — it is what makes the rule a decided property rather than an inference from absence, which the task rails forbid.

VOCABULARY, re-measured: `FOUNDATION_DISPATCH_EVENT_TYPES` (foundation-attempt-contracts.ts:47) = `{RECORDED: "FoundationAttemptRecorded", RESERVED: "FoundationDispatchReserved"}`; `FOUNDATION_DISPATCH_COMMAND_KIND` = "foundation.dispatch" (:39). `commitFoundationPhase` (foundation-attempt-store.ts:99) writes both with `tag: "RECORDED" | "RESERVED"` onto `bound.target`, event id `${grantId}:${tag}`, correlation `${correlationId}:${tag}`. There is no third phase and no separate PHASE vocabulary — `grep -rn "PHASE|Phase" foundation-attempt-contracts.ts` returns nothing.

THE GAP IS STILL OPEN: `InFlightAttempt` = `{attemptRef, situation}` (restart-reconciliation.ts:32) with ZERO producers.

EXISTING DECODE DISCIPLINE to reuse rather than re-derive: `readStoredFoundationAttempt` (:128) filters RECORDED, refuses `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_AMBIGUOUS` on more than one, `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_ABSENT` on none, decodes, RE-ENCODES and byte-compares, refusing `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_DRIFT` on mismatch (:135-141). `readFoundationReservationDigest` (:115) requires exactly one RESERVED and answers null otherwise. The enumerator must be no laxer on either.

THE N+1 TRAP AND ITS FIX. The obvious implementation pages reservations then calls a per-attempt reader for each — one round trip per reservation. `StoredEvent` carries `aggregateId`, so the correct shape is TWO type-filtered walks (RESERVED and RECORDED) set-differenced by aggregateId. Task-69c2c9e7 landed `readEventsByTypeAfter` (sqlite-event-store.ts:354, delegate at decision-ledger.ts:77/148) index-backed by `domain_events_event_type_position`, so both walks are bounded and index-backed.

`situation` is typed `unknown` because `classifyCrash` validates it internally — not licence to pass a caller value through. Populate from the decoded reservation's committed fields (requestDigest, sessionId, recordVersion are what `commitFoundationPhase`'s reservation payload carries).
planningNotes.risks:
1) THE RULE MUST BE CITED, NOT JUST IMPLEMENTED. Without the `foundation-attempt-service.ts:218-224` citation in the module header, the next reader sees a reservation-minus-record difference and cannot tell whether it was reasoned from production or guessed — and the task rails specifically forbid guessing it.

2) THE N+1 SHAPE PASSES EVERY CORRECTNESS TEST. It returns exactly the right attempts; only the cost assertion distinguishes it. So that assertion must carry a literal bound tight enough to fail the full-stream and per-reservation shapes, and step 3 requires verifying it reddens against a deliberately-wrong version BEFORE the real one is written. Drill 4 re-proves it after.

3) SKIPPING A DRIFTED OR DUPLICATED ATTEMPT LOSES WORK SILENTLY. It is the natural way to keep the sweep "working", and it means an attempt nobody reconciles. Refuse with the codes the existing readers already fix; drills 2 and 3 guard both.

4) A LAXER DECODE THAN THE EXISTING READERS. `readStoredFoundationAttempt` re-encodes and byte-compares before trusting a payload. An enumerator that merely decodes would admit records the single-attempt path rejects, so the sweep and the reader would disagree about the same bytes.

5) `situation` PROVENANCE. Typed `unknown` because `classifyCrash` validates it — easy to read as "anything goes". A caller value or a clock reading reaching it would let the sweep classify a crash from data the crash did not produce.

6) CONSUMER-EDGE DISCIPLINE: do not edit restart-reconciliation.ts, foundation-attempt-store.ts or foundation-attempt-contracts.ts. This module is additive; report blocked rather than editing a producer.
